source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Verify the patient with two person-specific identifiers and label the specimen container with the required identifiers in the patient's presence.","B":"Label the blood tubes at the nurses' station after leaving the room, then compare the labels with the electronic chart before sending them.","C":"Prelabel blood tubes before seeing the patient because matching the labels to the room assignment at collection is an acceptable identification method.","D":"Use the patient's room number as one of the two identifiers because room assignment is considered a reliable person-specific identifier."}}
source_row.rationale: Joint Commission guidance requires reliable patient identification and specimen labeling with two identifiers in the patient's presence. Option A is correct. Option B delays labeling until after leaving the patient. Option C describes prelabeling blood tubes before seeing the patient, which Joint Commission specifically identifies as unacceptable. Option D is incorrect because room number is not a person-specific identifier.
source_row.source_detail: The Joint Commission — Two Patient Identifiers: Understanding the Requirements, FAQ updated 2026-04-21: use at least two person-specific identifiers; specimen containers must be labeled with two identifiers in the patient's presence; prelabeling blood tubes before seeing the patient is not acceptable; room number/location is not an acceptable identifier. Joint Commission standards FAQ last updated 2026-04-21; current requirements live-rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Safety and Infection Prevention and Control: patient identification, specimen collection, asepsis, high-alert medication safeguards, fall prevention and communication that prevents safety events as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
